Following the Clone Wars, in the [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility|Mustafarian mining facility]] of Mustafar, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker—who had fallen to the dark side as Sidious' new apprentice Darth Vader—[[Duel on Mustafar|dueled each other]] and made their way into the [[Separatist Council war room|war room]] and momentarily into a nearby [[Separatist Council Conference Room|conference room]]. During the duel with his former apprentice,{{Film|III}} feeling his former friend's focused hatred was horrifying, as Kenobi had felt it from Ventress, Dooku, Maul, and Opress.{{EncyclopediaCite|The End of the Clone Wars}} ===A new life=== ====Peace and quiet==== {{Quote|The peace and quiet appeals to me. That's why I took the job.''"
"''This appeals to you? This doesn't appeal to me, and I live here.|Asajj Ventress and Cort|}} [[File:Business_matters.png|thumb|250px|right|Ventress took a simple job as a security guard for Cort.]] The end of the Clone Wars saw the defeat of the Separatists following the deaths of Dooku and Grievous. The victorious Republic was [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire]] under Palpatine as the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]], and the Jedi and other Force-sensitive individuals were [[Great Jedi Purge|hunted]] down by Imperials. Ventress chose to leave her old life behind in favor of a simple job as a security guard for a human woman named [[Cort]] in a [[Cort's transport office|transport office]] at a [[spaceport]] on an [[Unidentified astronomical object (Cort)|astronomical object]]. At one point, she kicked a [[Unidentified Rodian transport office customer|Rodian]] out of the office when he pulled a blaster on Cort and demanded transport without sufficient funding. Ventress' adept combat abilities caused Cort to be puzzled as to why she would choose such a menial job; Ventress explained that it was the life she wanted. [[File:InquisitorClashAsajjVentress-AWayForward.png|thumb|250px|left|Ventress was forced to draw her lightsaber while assisting Lyco Strata.]] Soon after, [[Lyco Strata]], a young survivor of [[Order 66]], entered Ventress' workplace, attempting to [[Hunt for Lyco Strata|evade]] the Empire's forces. Ventress realized his status as a Jedi fugitive when he tried and failed to perform a [[Mind trick|Jedi mind trick]] on Cort to gain passage without enough money. Ventress began to escort him outside, but she sheltered him when several [[stormtrooper]]s and a [[Viper probe droid]] approached and entered the building. She performed a successful mind trick on the [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Asajj Ventress)|lead stormtrooper]], convincing him that nothing was amiss there and to search [[Docking Bay 24 (Ventress)|Docking Bay 24]] instead. However, Cort gave up Strata's hiding spot upon hearing the possibility of a reward, forcing Ventress and Strata to draw their lightsabers and kill the Imperials present. A frustrated Ventress then led Strata away, abandoning her simple security guard life. ====Helping Strata==== [[File:RazziHighsingerVentressTogetherAgain-TotUFriends.png|thumb|250px|right|Ventress meet with Razzi and Highsinger for intel on the Hidden Path.]] Ventress went on to help Strata escape from the Imperials, including an [[Unidentified Inquisitor (Asajj Ventress)|Inquisitor]], whom she was bested by but saved from by Strata. The two evaded the Stormtroopers and snuck onto a [[Lau cargo ship]]. Once inside the [[Freighter|cargo ship]], Ventress revealed her identity. Searching for information on Vos, Ventress met up with her old bounty hunter acquaintances Latts Razzi and C-21 Highsinger on a terrestrial [[Unidentified world (Latts Razzi)|planet]] with a [[Unidentified bustling city|bustling city]]. The two took a [[Star Commuter 2000]] shuttle to a planet where Ventress heard her old acquaintances had information on the Path. After stopping a [[Unidentified four-armed alien|four-armed alien]], from killing Razzi, Ventress asks about the Hidden Path, and both Razzi and Highsinger agreed to trade her intel on the Path in exchange for her and Strata's help on a [[Heist at Cassaro shipyard|heist]] at an [[Cassaro shipyard|Imperial shipyard]] on the planet [[Cassaro]]. Although Highsinger was caught, forcing the group to fight off the stormtroopers, Ventress manage to help the three escape by cutting a cable holding a [[ISD-72x shield generator dome]] so the three used it to escape to [[Latts Razzi's ship|Razzi's ship]]. Because Strata lost the shield relay unit, Razzi later betrayed Ventress, having learned Strata was a Jedi and wanting to cash in on the bounty for him, Ventress defeated her old collaborator and forced her to give them the intel. Razzi did so, dropping the two off in a spaceport in the bustling city{{TOTU|Friends}} and Ventress and Strata then departed for a [[Unidentified desert world|desert world]]. ====Making peace==== [[File:OneWarriortoAnother-EpisodeThumb.png|thumb|250px|left|Ventress helped a former Separatist ally and local raiders make peace.]] After arriving on the planet, the two made their way into the desert to search for the Hidden Path, eventually stumbling upon a [[Unidentified grandfather's farm|homestead]], where they encountered an [[Unidentified grandfather (Asajj Ventress)|elderly human man]] and his [[Unidentified granddaughter|granddaughter]]. The two homesteaders welcomed the travelers into their home and revealed that they were low on [[water]] due to attacks by raiders. While Ventress was initially reluctant to disclose her true identity, she was recognized by the old man, who revealed himself to be a former Separatist war hero and and addressed her as "Lady Ventress." Lyco asked for directions to [[Cipher Canyon]], to which the man said that it would be difficult to find as it was not on any map. Ventress and Lyco prepare to leave, but before they could do so, the elderly veteran offered to let his granddaughter guide them to Cipher Canyon, as it was not far from the [[Unidentified spring (Cipher Canyon)|spring]] where they fetch water. While attempting to retrieve water along with the homesteader's granddaughter, they were attacked by a band of these raiders. Although they tried to fight them off at first, Lyco was able to understand [[Unidentified species (Cipher Canyon)|the species']] language, allowing them to come to an uneasy truce and return to the farmer's homestead, intending to make peace. When they arrived, Lyco revealed that he was a Jedi, and the old man threatened him with his blaster; however, Ventress told him that Lyco was her friend, causing him to stand down. With one of the raiders leading them to Cipher Canyon, they come upon a large number of people lining up to board a starship. Though Strata tried to invite Ventress to come with him, suggesting she could reunite with Quinlan Vos, she ultimately declined, reasoning that she had moved on, and that Strata's path was as a Jedi. Though she rides away believing that Lyco has left aboard the [[GX1 short hauler]], she was soon interrupted by Lyco, who revealed that he had decided to stay with her. ===The clones=== {{Quote|I just finished a job with some clones. They were asking about the Empire's M-count bounties. What can you tell me? I'm sure you can track them down easily enough. I'll send you what I have.|Fennec Shand, to Ventress|{{TBB|Bad Territory}}}} [[File:VentressShipFront.png|right|thumb|350px|Ventress returned to bounty hunting and obtained a new starship.]] After her encounters with Strata,{{SW|url=news/who-is-ventress|text=Who Is Asajj Ventress?}} states that the events of ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Underworld|Tales of the Underworld]]'' featuring Asajj Ventress take place prior to her meeting the [[Clone Force 99|Bad Batch]]. Ventress covertly continued her travels on a [[Ventress' ship|personal starship]].{{TBB|The Harbinger}} The Separatists were defeated following the deaths of Dooku and Grievous and the victorious Republic was [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire]] under Palpatine as the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]]. The Jedi and other Force-sensitive individuals were [[Great Jedi Purge|hunted]] down by Imperials, including clone troopers as they were obliged to be loyal to the Emperor via their [[Behavioral modification biochip|inhibitor chips]].''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' Around [[18 BBY]], the Empire would post bounties on individuals with high "M-counts"—a measurement of [[midi-chlorian]]s in the blood which indicated the host's potential to channel the Force. At one point, Ventress took on a M-count job. Eventually, the rogue clones of [[Clone Force 99]], also known as the Bad Batch, found that one of their members, [[Omega]], was being targeted by the Empire as an M-count target. Hoping to learn more, the clones [[Hunter]] and [[Wrecker]] thus contacted the bounty hunter [[Fennec Shand]] for information. Because Ventress had previously taken on one of the M-count bounty jobs, Shand—who was a contact of Ventress—passed on the Bad Batch's details to her, knowing that she had more information. Ventress then tracked the clones to their [[Pabu island|island shelter]] on the isolated planet [[Pabu]]. ====Before sunset==== {{Quote|I wasn't planning on killing you, but you're making it very tempting.|Asajj Ventress|}} [[File:AsajjVentress-TBBs3trailer.png|thumb|left|275px|Asajj Ventress facing the Bad Batch]] After Ventress landed her ship in a [[Pabu cove|cavern]], several [[Moonyo|moon-yos]] and Omega's [[lurca hound]] companion, [[Batcher]], were attracted to the cave. Omega stumbled upon Ventress, who stopped the young girl from running away while Batcher called the rest of the Batch, consisting of Hunter, Wrecker, and [[Crosshair]], to the cave. As the clones confronted her, Ventress asked why they wanted to know about the Empire's M-count bounties, cautioning them that they were "reckless" in seeking the information and should be laying low. The clones were reluctant to reveal their suspicion that Omega herself was being targeted for her M-count, but Omega wanted Ventress to test her M-count, insisting that she wanted to know who she really was. Ventress agreed, beginning to give Omega three tests with a balancing task. Standing on a slippery rock on one leg, Omega was unable to let go of her conscious mind and continued slipping. When Ventress sensed the other clones realized her identity as a former Separatist assassin, she sent Omega to retrieve a white blossom from the [[weeping maya tree]] at the top of the island before sunset—which was quickly approaching. With Omega gone, Ventress faced the other clones, who demanded that she leave. However, Ventress was insistent on staying and warned the clones against attacking her, to no avail. After defeating the three clones, Ventress reiterated that times had changed in the new [[Imperial Era|age of the Empire]]. Omega returned with her flower to find her brothers defeated at the hands of Ventress. As the former Sith used the Force to choke Wrecker, Omega pleaded for Ventress to stop. When Hunter told Omega that Ventress was a war criminal, Ventress angrily replied that they were not enemies, as they had all been pawns during the war, regardless of which side they had served before stalking away. ====Waves==== {{Dialogue|Crosshair|I still can't figure out what side you're on.|Ventress|My own.|Hunter|You're not worried about the Empire coming after you?|Ventress|They can try. But I've got a few lives left.|attr=The Bad Batch questions Ventress's actions before she leaves Pabu|src=}} Later, Ventress and the clones parted. Hunter, Wrecker, and Crosshair warned Omega that Ventress had committed deadly acts of violence during the war, yet Omega was adamant that Ventress should be given a chance, just as how she had never given up hope on Crosshair, who previously betrayed the squad. The next day, with the Batch having promised Omega not to interfere, the young girl met Ventress at the island's sea port. Omega expressed her appreciation that Ventress wanted to help her, since she remained on the island. The pair then took a [[boat]] and went out to sea. [[File:VratheanSurfaces-Harbinger.png|thumb|right|350px|A vrathean surfaces while Ventress and Omega are at sea.]] After traveling a distance from Pabu island, Ventress instructed Omega to reach out, since individuals who used the Force often had an affinity with animals. Omega thought the exercise to be meaningless, but Ventress herself reached out in the Force, [[Taming beasts|attracting]] several [[Luminescent green ray|green rays]] in the sea to their boat. Omega was amazed by Ventress' abilities until a large [[vrathean]] then appeared and capsized the boat. As Ventress and Omega landed in the water, the young girl was grabbed by one of the vrathean's tentacles, but Ventress quickly used her lightsaber to free her. The Batch attempted to battle the creature with their [[Marauder (Omicron-class)|starship]], but Ventress growled that they were hindering her efforts to calm the beast. Omega persuaded her companions to trust Ventress and stop firing, even as Ventress herself was being grabbed by the vrathean. Ventress reached out to the creature, who calmed as the pair formed a connection. The vrathean then gently put Ventress down and left the scene, allowing the clones' ship to lower. At the ramp, Crosshair offered a hand to pick up Omega and then Ventress as well. The group returned to the cave, where Ventress told Omega that she did not have a high midi-chlorian count before parting. With Omega gone with Batcher and Wrecker, Hunter, with [[Crosshair]] flanking him, accused Ventress of lying. She replied that if a person had high Force potential, they must be properly trained to make use of it, and that the Empire would hunt down those strong in the Force. She also advised the clones to hide elsewhere, and, upon being asked whose side she was on and whether she was afraid of the Empire, stated that she was on her own and had a few more lives. Ventress then boarded her ship and flew away. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Next you're going to tell me that you weren't planning to mention Captain Rex, Ahsoka, Ventress, Cad Bane, Savage Opress, Jar Jar, and the Mandalorians?"
"Well... I guess I could always go back and tell their stories later."
"Out of order?|A Whill, to [[Unidentified Whill|another]]|{{StoryCite|story=Whills (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} Ventress proved to be remembered long after the Clone Wars. Her image was printed upon a playing card included in a set that also used an image of Sidious. During the [[mutiny on Mon Cala]], a group of four [[stormtrooper]]s were in the middle of a card game, with both the Sidious and Ventress cards in one trooper's hand. However, their game was interrupted when [[Han Solo]] and [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] breached the room and stunned the four soldiers.[[Star Wars (2015) 47|''Star Wars'' (2015) 47]] Ventress and Vos's [[rescue of Marg Krim's family]] was mentioned in "[[Index of Organizations]]," a survival compendium sent out by [[Carson Teva]] during the [[New Republic Era]], where it described the two as "unidentified Force users."{{GermanFanCite|115|Database}} Sometime after the [[Galactic Civil War]]'s [[Battle of Endor]], she was mentioned by a [[Unidentified second Whill|member]] of the [[Whills]] as someone to be remembered in [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]]. ==Personality and traits== ===Disciple of darkness=== {{Quote|You've never been afraid of anything, Asajj Ventress.''"
"''You're wrong. I was terrified.''"
"''Of what?''"
"''Of losing you. I've been lying for so long. It's second nature to me. We learned to trust each other, but what I felt…I was so scared. I was afraid to tell you about Tholme because I thought you'd hate me. I'd only just learned how to trust and care about someone again, and I…I couldn't bear the thought that if you really knew me, knew what I had done, you'd despise me.|Quinlan Vos and Ventress|}} Ventress was a Dathomirian female who stood at 1.78 [[meter]]s (5 [[Foot|feet]], 10 inches) - 1.79 meters tall, with brown, later silver-blonde [[hair]], ice-blue [[eye]]s and bone-white skin with purple tattoos. [[File:TwinStrike-Convergence.png|thumb|left|260px|Once a disciple of the light, Ventress gave into anger after the death of her master.]] As a child Ventress was kind and caring, but became dark and brooding after the death of her master, Ky Narec. Giving in to rage and resentment, she subsequently spiraled into darkness and developed a strong will to survive. For a time, she heard the voice of Narec in her mind, urging her away from the dark side. However, after learning Narec had been the one who killed Hal'Sted, she rejected his guidance, giving herself fully to her anger. She grew to believe that the Jedi Code and Jedi disciplines were overrated lies that prevented someone from achieving full power. Because of this, she believed the Jedi would not be able to stop her and believed selflessness made one vulnerable. Known to be quick to anger, Ventress could easily be infuriated, such as when her formidable lightsaber skills were described to her as those of an amateur by Luminara Unduli. Despite her quick temper, she was very cunning and swift, allowing her to outsmart most foes. She also had a modicum of respect for her opponents, believing Aayla Secura deserved a dignified death. Ventress could also be vindictive and inconsiderate. After being betrayed, abandoned and nearly killed by Dooku, Ventress desired to kill him and went to the Nightsisters to find a way to defeat her former master. She recruited Savage Opress and treated him like a slave, which ultimately caused him to turn against her. ===Attachment, loss, and letting go=== {{Quote|You've told me your existence has been nothing but pain and loss. Never feeling secure. Never having a home. You deserve so much, and I can get it for us. The life we'll be able to have together once—''"
"''What kind of life will that be, Quinlan? The kind where we're slaves to our hatred? Our rage? That's what the dark side made me. That's what it ''does''. Nothing is ever enough. You get more, and more, but you're never happy. It's a trap baited with all the things you want most in life—and it's not worth living. I already left that behind.|Quinlan Vos and Asajj Ventress|}} After becoming a bounty hunter, her attitude softened somewhat, as seen when she allowed Pluma Sodi to return to her people. Likewise, she lost interest in killing some of her former enemies, including Obi-Wan Kenobi and Ahsoka Tano. In fact, she rescued Kenobi from Darth Maul and Opress, more interested in the latter's bounty reward than her previous enmity with the Jedi Master. On the other hand, she helped Tano, as she empathized with the Padawan's situation, likening it to her own with Count Dooku. She also incapacitated a group of clones without seriously harming any of them, and implied that not killing people was her new modus operandi. As she distanced herself more and more from her time under Dooku, Ventress, to highlight her misunderstood status, used a snake as the icon on her bounty hunter armor; they were thought to be evil, even when they were not. [[File:Ventress_DD.png|thumb|right|250px|Ventress, neither Sith nor Jedi]] Glad to have a reason to have a new weapon after losing her red ones on Coruscant, she came to wield a unique lightsaber with a pale yellow blade. The color reassured Ventress that she had indeed left behind her life as a pawn of the Sith. Additionally, its yellow color equally showed her she had not been pushed towards the Jedi; Ventress' lightsaber showed she was no Jedi nor Sith, she was simply herself. During her encounter with Ohnaka Gang, Ventress changing her allegiances and lightsaber did nothing to make her less dangerous. She was also, to her surprise, happy to replace her old red lightsabers after spending a time inconvenienced by their loss. She also realized the red blades had been her last physical link to her time as Dooku's apprentice, and she was pleased to find her new lightsaber produced a pale yellow blade. Needing to pretend to be a captured Jedi to fool the Ohnaka Gang was not a part she was rather comfortable taking on, but she did so nevertheless, and her yellow lightsaber—the design of which was symbolic of her state of mind—made the act more convincing. Near the end of the war, as she traveled with Quinlan Vos to assassinate Count Dooku, her more compassionate and trusting side was even more strengthened—to the point of her developing a romantic attraction to him, with the two eventually becoming lovers. She sacrificed herself to save Vos, who was influenced by the dark side, fully redeeming herself into the light. ==Powers and abilities== ===Lightsaber abilities=== {{Quote|Do you think you'll still be able to call on the Force once I've separated your head from your body?''"
"''Even with my vision clouded, I recognize the fighting style of Count Dooku. Your version is unrefined, amateurish, ''sloppy''.|Ventress and Luminara Unduli|}} [[File:Asajj_Ventress_SoR.png|thumb|left|250px|Ventress was exceptionally skilled with her blades.]] Asajj Ventress was a master of [[Jar'Kai]], a style she acquired after the death of her first master, Ky Narec, taking up his lightsaber alongside her own. Under Count Dooku, the mechanisms in her new curved lightsabers enabled her to combine them into a bizarre, though effective, S-shaped [[Double-bladed lightsaber|double-bladed weapon]] known as a [[split saber]].''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' These red blades became her distinctive weapon. Under the tutelage of Dooku, Ventress learned to utilize [[Form II]]. However, her technique still was not without its flaws; notably her version was criticized by a temporarily blinded Luminara Unduli as being "unrefined," "amateurish," and "sloppy." By the time of their duel, Ventress had already developed a physical strength to hold up simultaneous bladelocks with multiple duelists at a time, and Ahsoka Tano recognized her as "too powerful for any one Jedi to fight alone." Aayla Secura also recognized that she had significant raw power. Ventress proved a match for both Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker in many of their encounters.''[[Star Wars: Women of the Galaxy]]'' On Teth, she disarmed Kenobi—a member of the Jedi Council—who later deprived her of one of her weapons in return. She was able to contend with General Grievous, as she gained the upper hand and cut one of his robotic arms in a lightsaber duel. She could throw her lightsaber and recall it back to her with the Force. In one instance, Ventress managed to wield her final lightsaber with both hands tied behind her back, all the while fighting off the Ohnaka Gang. Assisted by the Force, she detected the direction of blaster bolts and used the blade to deflect them as well as make physical contact with a few pirates. After being resurrected by Mother Talzin, Ventress' skills remained the same, as she was able to deflect blaster bolts from three [[Clone 99]]s. She was also able to fight an Inquisitor but ultimately was defeated, despite having help. During a heist at the Cassaro shipyard, Ventress manage to deflect many blaster bolts from Stormtroopers and even after being betrayed by Razzi and Highsinger, she manage to defeat Highsinger by cutting him across the torso and his right arm, which had a [[flamethrower]]. ===Force powers=== {{Quote|When Ky Narec was killed, I allowed my hatred to take over. Hatred gave me access to abilities the Jedi think are too unnatural. But the Sith know that hatred is the path to ultimate power.|Asajj Ventress|}} [[File:Force_Power_Bind_RotS.png|thumb|right|240px|Ventress Force-chokes two clone troopers while telekinetically lifting them in the air.]] Ventress was viewed by Obi-Wan Kenobi as having immense willpower, with more experience in the Force than many Jedi Knights. Darth Sidious himself sensed that the Dathomirian was growing more powerful and feared that his apprentice, Darth Tyranus, would use her to help overthrow him as Dark Lord of the Sith. All of this had been in due part to her close connection with the dark side. She did not often employ the taming beasts power but could successfully use it. Ventress displayed a great aptitude for [[Force jump|Force-enhanced jumps]], frequently employing them during her duels. She was also skilled with telekinesis, as witnessed when she lifted Captain Rex in the air, while simultaneously choking him. Later, the assassin proved herself capable of Force-choking and telekinetically levitating Skywalker and Kenobi simultaneously, when fueled by her rage, pain and desperation. Shortly after, she used that same power on Ratch and his three men, this time achieving a lethal result. Ventress demonstrated an aptitude for using mind tricks, though Rex was able to avoid her influence when contacting Skywalker. ===Other skills=== Ventress displayed skills in unarmed combat, being able to easily fight a group of Nightbrothers when she was looking for a suitable servant on Dathomir. Her [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]] skills were later displayed when she fought Savage Opress and Maul alongside Kenobi, dodging Opress' aggressive blows and striking back with a flurry of punches and kicks until Kenobi returned her lightsaber to her. She was able to fight Hunter, Crosshair, and Wrecker, ultimately triumphing against all three Clone 99s. While working as a security guard for Cort, she was able to disarm a Rodian customer and send him out. Ventress also demonstrated piloting skills when flying a ''Ginivex''-class fanblade starfighter and the ''Banshee'', a [[Lancer-class pursuit craft|''Lancer''-class pursuit craft]].{{FFGXW2|set=Scum and Villainy Conversion Kit|cardname=Asajj Ventress}} She was also known for her superb agility which made her a dangerous duelist, which came handy on many missions, such as evading Dooku's attacks when she, Karis and Naa'leth infiltrated Castle Serenno. ==Equipment== [[File:AsajjVentressSeason5-TCWCEJtB.png|left|thumb|190px|Ventress during her time as a bounty hunter]] As a Jedi, Ventress used a green-bladed lightsaber during her apprenticeship under Ky Narec. After Narec was shot and killed by a Weequay pirate raider in battle, Ventress took up her master's own green-bladed lightsaber together with her own to enact her vengeance upon the raiders. Dooku later gave her two red [[curved-hilt lightsaber]]s as a gift upon taking her on as his own Sith apprentice. Ventress' twin red sabers could connect to form a saberstaff. Later, when Ventress and her clan sisters attempted to assassinate Dooku for betraying and abandoning her, she wielded a Jedi lightsaber with a blue blade, one that was provided to her by Mother Talzin in order to convince Dooku that the infiltrators and would-be assassins were Jedi. During her career as a bounty hunter, she used a full face mask with a voice modulator, but lost this along with her dual red lightsabers to Barriss Offee. Ventress later acquired for herself a new yellow-bladed lightsaber from the black market. The yellow lightsaber's design provided a great deal of information about Ventress' own state of being. Ventress typically wore the weapon openly, though during the mission to infiltrate Dooku's high society gala on to Raxus she strapped the blade to her upper left thigh, concealed under her dress. Nevertheless, she continued her tradition of being nothing if not practical through its design, as she could easily reach the lightsaber hilt through a side seam. During the Imperial Era, she wielded a new yellow lightsaber with a curved hilt akin to her red lightsabers' hilts. During the Imperial Era, she also carried new gear with a [[blaster pistol]] of an unknown model with a [[scope]] mounted on the side in a [[holster]] on her right hip and small [[backpack]]. She also kelp her [[snake]] symbol on her left shoulder. ==Behind the scenes== ===Conception and design=== [[File:Assajj_concept-art.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Asajj Ventress concept art]] Asajj Ventress debuted in the current [[canon]] continuity in the [[2008]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' series, in which she was voiced by [[Nika Futterman]]. Futterman knew only as much as the audience regarding the character and for her portrayal simply assumed that Ventress had a difficult childhood. The character was created for the [[2003]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] animated television series ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''. The name "Ventress" was suggested by [[Samuel C. Spitale]], naming her after the [[Wikipedia:Ventress, Louisiana|town of Ventress]] in the [[Wikipedia:United States|US]] state of [[Wikipedia:Louisiana|Louisiana]] because it reminded him of "the voodoo queen" [[Wikipedia:Marie Laveau|Marie Laveau]].{{Twitter|SamuelCSpitale|status/1404156693009690624|[[Samuel C. Spitale]]|quote=Indeed! Named after the town Ventress in Louisiana. I wanted a word reminiscent of Marie Laveau, the voodoo queen. And Ventress fit the bill.}} Her first name, "Asajj," was proposed by [[Leland Chee]] after the character Asaji (浅茅) from [[Wikipedia:Akira Kurosawa|Akira Kurosawa's]] 1957 film [[Wikipedia:Throne of Blood|''Throne of Blood'']], in turn based on [[Wikipedia:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare's]] [[Wikipedia:Lady Macbeth|Lady Macbeth]] from the 17th-century play [[Wikipedia:Macbeth|''Macbeth'']].{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=93010&start=4935#5509733|thread=Welcome some BCaT VIPs|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2003-12-19|time=3:02 PM|quote=On occasion, Licensing is asked to come up with names, as was the case of Durge and Asajj Ventress. If I recall correctly, Haden Blackman named Durge. Since you ask, I suggested the first name "Asajj" which sounds alot like "Asaji," the "Lady Macbeth" character from Akira Kurowsawa's ''Throne of Blood''.}} Her design originated as concept art by [[Dermot Power]] for a potential female Sith Lord during the development of the [[2002]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. However, the character was abandoned in favor of Count Dooku{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/nightsisters-trivia-gallery|text="Nightsisters" Trivia Gallery}} upon the casting of [[Christopher Lee]] in that role. Power wanted the Sith's earlier designs to look almost as if she was a samurai.''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]'' [[File:BountyHunterMask-SoH.png|thumb|left|250px|Ventress' bounty hunter helmet was designed by several people]] Ventress' costume at the beginning of ''The Clone Wars ''episode "[[Nightsisters (episode)|Nightsisters]]" was a direct recreation of the outfit she wore in her initial concept art and early ''Legends'' appearances. [[Chris Glenn]] designed her costume for the episode "[[Bounty (episode)|Bounty]]." The outfit was accented with leggings with a pattern that resembled the red piping on [[Han Solo]]'s trousers. The shoulder plate of the costume had an illustration of a black snake that represented Ventress' character as a misunderstood creature that is commonly assumed to be dangerous.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bounty-trivia-gallery|text="Bounty" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}} The helmet worn by Ventress in the ''Clone Wars ''episode "[[To Catch a Jedi]]" was designed by [[Dave Filoni]], Chris Glenn, and [[Darren Marshall]].{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/to-catch-a-jedi-trivia-gallery|text="To Catch a Jedi" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 4}} In ''Legends'', Ventress first encountered [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] during a [[duel on Yavin 4]], while Skywalker and Kenobi's first encounter with Ventress in canon was part of a mission to Cato Neimoidia in the novel [[Brotherhood (novel)|''Brotherhood'']]. However, author [[Mike Chen (author)|Mike Chen]] revealed that Skywalker's mention of fighting other agents of Dooku by that point can be read as a reference to the Yavin 4 duel; as Chen explained, the duel can still have happened in canon, but Skywalker was unable to see his opponent was Ventress because of the rain and darkness around them.{{WebCite|url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/star-wars-anakin-skywalker-clone-wars-canon-twist-brotherhood-book|text=Star Wars writer reveals a new Anakin canon twist|author=[https://www.inverse.com/profile/ryan-britt-18846684 Britt, Ryan]|date=2022-05-11|archivedate=20220512022248}} Indeed, in ''Brotherhood'', Skywalker also notes that he thinks he has seen Ventress' fanblade starfighter before, and Ventress displays a familiarity with him by revealing that she knows his name, much to Skywalker's surprise. ===''Dark Disciple''=== ''Dark Disciple'', the 2015 novel focusing on the character, is based upon eight episodes planned for the unfinished seventh and eighth seasons of ''The Clone Wars''. The first illustration showing Ventress with her hair grown out was also developed for the series. Dave Filoni explained Ventress' shaved head symbolized her loyalty to the Sith philosophy.{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-clone-wars-season-7-ventress-novel|text='Star Wars: Clone Wars' Returns For Season 7 (in Book Form)|author=Dyce, Andrew|work=ScreenRant|archivedate=20190403134138}} [[File:Ventress_lightsaber_concept_art.png|thumb|right|250px|Ventress' yellow lightsaber]] Ventress' yellow lightsaber was designed by [[Will Nichols]] for the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series. It was scheduled to appear in eight episodes starring Ventress and [[Quinlan Vos]]. The show was canceled, however, before the episodes were finished and the story was instead adapted into the novel ''[[Dark Disciple]]'' by [[Christie Golden]]. Nichols posted the concept design of the lightsaber in his portfolio in 2016.{{ArtStation|username=songjong|url=artwork/Zx0zw|name=William Nichols|text=Star Wars Clone Wars Props}} The lightsaber's concept design{{ArtStation|username=songjong|url=artwork/Zx0zw|name=William Nichols|text=Star Wars Clone Wars Props}} was later used in the revived [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|Season 7]] of ''The Clone Wars'', being used as half of [[Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber|Maul's lightsaber]].{{TCW|The Phantom Apprentice}} ===Fate and future=== {{Quote|We don't want to spoil anything, but want fans to know that any new storytelling with Ventress will align with the events of ''Star Wars: Dark Disciple''.|[[Brad Rau]], on ''The Bad Batch'' Season 3|}} After Futterman returned to work with Filoni, voicing the character [[Presence]] for the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[Twilight of the Apprentice]]" in [[2016]], Filoni commented on her role by saying that although he was "never going to bring back Ventress," he was happy to find a way to give Futterman a role in the show.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2016/03/31/star-wars-rebels-dave-filoni-on-ahsokas-fate-mauls-return-and-much-more|text=Star Wars Rebels: Dave Filoni on Ahsoka's Fate, Maul's Return and Much More|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2016-03-31|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archivedate=20160401045238}} Despite these comments, Filoni later considered options for the Sith to return in later animation projects, pitching her to appear in episodes of ''[[Star Wars Resistance]]''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/star-wars-resistance-kylo-ren-asajj-ventress|text=Star Wars Resistance Nearly Pitted Kylo Ren Against Asajj Ventress|author=[https://www.cbr.com/author/ndom Dominguez, Noah]|date=2021-09-02|work=[https://web.archive.org/web/20210910075833/https://www.cbr.com CBR.com]|archivedate=20210910075833}} At one point, Ventress was written into a version of the episode "[[The Relic Raiders]]," where she was going to be revealed to have survived her fate in ''Dark Disciple''. In this appearance she would have dueled [[Supreme Leader]] [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]. However, her role was later changed to accommodate the original character [[Mika Grey]] instead. ''Resistance'' writer and executive producer [[Brandon Auman]] admitted that he initially thought that Filoni may have been joking about the idea before realizing that it was a serious suggestion. As Auman worked on the script for the episode "[[The Relic Raiders]]," Ventress remained in the story's plans until near the end, when she was ultimately written out in favor of Grey.{{WookYouTube|ML1nYpSU0d0|Wookieepedia Interviews - Brandon Auman}} Filoni's reasoning for ultimately not including Ventress was based around the notion that Ventress' appearance would take too much attention away from the main cast. Eventually, Ventress would make her return to animation with [[2024]]'s [[The Bad Batch Season 3|''The Bad Batch'' Season 3]], which would align with previous storytelling from ''Dark Disciple'', in which she apparently died.{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-season-3-trailer|text=Watch the ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season 3 Trailer}} Her [[Databank (2014-)|Databank entry]] on [[StarWars.com]] was updated, removing the mention of her "giving her life" to instead more vaguely note she "sacrificed herself" by taking most of Dooku's Force lightning. The entry teased her return by noting that her sacrifice was not the end of her story. In an interview with ''TheDirect'', ''Bad Batch'' Supervising Director [[Brad Rau]], after once more affirming they would not contradict ''Dark Disciple'', teased that Ventress could return in future projects: he stated that ''The Bad Batch'' would not answer every question fans had and that those may instead be addressed in other stories.{{WebCite|url=https://thedirect.com/article/star-wars-asajj-ventress-appearances-future-bad-batch-exclusive|text=Star Wars Producers Tease More Asajj Ventress Appearances After The Bad Batch (Exclusive)|author=Russ Milheim|archiveurl=https://archive.is/RC3KH}} This later became true through the ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Underworld|Tales of the Underworld]]''. ===Other appearances=== Asajj Ventress also appeared in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'', developed by [[EA Capital Games]],''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' being present at it's lauch in late [[2015]].{{EA|url=games/starwars/galaxy-of-heroes/news/title-update-and-10-year-anniversary-announcement|text=Title Update and 10-Year Anniversary Announcement Post}} Beginning in early [[2020]],{{ArtStation|username=davegibbons|name=[[Dave Gibbons (video game artist)|Dave Gibbons]]|url=artwork/WBe15E|text=Character Reworks|date=2024-05-16}} the game's older characters were redesigned to a more "realistic" artstyle and higher visual fidelity. Ventress' model was remastered by Senior Character Artist [[Thomas Guillory]] in a period of around three weeks and Guillory tried to reimagine what she would look like in live-action.{{ArtStation|username=nevermind3d|name=[[Thomas Guillory]]|url=artwork/98260L|text=Ventress|date=2025-05-15}} A second version of Ventress based on her look in ''Dark Disciple'' was later added to ''Galaxy of Heroes'' together with other characters inspired by ones present at the lauch for the game's ten year anniversary update in late [[2025]]. The new version was again designed by Guillory, inspired by the previous version.{{ArtStation|username=nevermind3d|name=[[Thomas Guillory]]|url=artwork/nJR4Q9|text=Dark Disciple Ventress|date=2025-11-21}} ===Contradictions=== [[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 112|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' Part 112]] states that Ventress built and designed the yellow lightsaber she wielded in the novel. According to it, after she acquired the kyber crystal under unknown means, the kyber, as always, had taken its color from the emotions of its wielder, which was why it was yellow. However, ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' later confirmed she did indeed secure the yellow lightsaber on the black market, as she had claimed in ''Dark Disciple''. In its "100 Best Ever Heroes and Villains" feature, in which it ranked Ventress among the 100 greatest characters to exist within the [[prequel trilogy]] era, [[Star Wars Adventures 12 (magazine)|''Star Wars Adventures'' 12]] mistakenly claims Ventress ended her journey as a Jedi Padawan,[[Star Wars Adventures 12 (magazine)|''Star Wars Adventures'' 12]] when in fact she was a But without it, we clones wouldn't exist.|Rex, on being a clone trooper|{{TCW|Shattered}}}} '''Clone troopers''', also known as '''Clone soldiers''', '''Republic troopers''', '''Republic troops''', '''Republic soldiers''', '''Regs''', and nicknamed the "'''Boys in White'''," were highly trained [[soldier]]s in the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]. Representing the future of [[Galaxy|galactic]] warfare, [[Cloning|clones]] were designed to be far superior to [[battle droid]]s. During the [[Republic Era|last years]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], clones formed the backbone of the [[Republic Military]], which waged war against the [[Separatist Droid Army|droid armies]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The [[Clone Wars]] were named after the Republic's clone [[army]], which became symbolic of the conflict that had spread throughout [[the galaxy]] after a [[millennium]] of [[Republic Era|peace]]. Clone [[trooper]]s were grown on the [[planet]] [[Kamino]] at the request of [[Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas]], who commissioned the [[Kaminoan]]s to build an army for the Republic. After Sifo Dyas' [[death]], the project was taken over by the [[Sith]]. Clones were modeled on a [[human]] [[Clone template|template]], the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett]], although their [[DNA|genetic structure]] was modified to make them less independent and more docile than their progenitor. They were also designed to age at twice the rate of [[Reproduction|natural]] humans, accelerating their growth and making them ready for combat in a [[Standard decade|decade's]] [[time]]. As the [[Separatist Crisis]] gave way to open war, the [[Galactic Senate]] empowered [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] to call the clone troopers into action, leading to their debut on the [[First Battle of Geonosis|battlefield]] of [[Geonosis]]. For three [[Standard year|years]], clones fought the Separatist [[droid]]s on all fronts across the galaxy. They were loyal to their [[Jedi General]]s and the Supreme Chancellor; though some clones questioned their service, leading to isolated cases of [[Cut Lawquane|desertion]] and [[Slick|treason]], most were proud to serve the Republic as it was the only life they had ever known. [[Timeline of galactic history|Galactic history]] was forever changed by a hidden [[behavioral modification biochip]] implanted in every clone, which was part of the Sith's plot to destroy the Jedi. Chancellor Palpatine, [[Duel in Palpatine's office|discovered]] by the [[Jedi]] to be the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Sidious, as well as the reason behind the Clone Wars, branded the Jedi as the [[Treason|enemies of the state]] and issued [[Order 66]], with the latter being a call for the [[Great Jedi Purge|annihilation]] of the [[Jedi Order]]. All across the galaxy, the clones turned against their [[general]]s, slaughtering them and [[Operation: Knightfall|storming]] the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]] under the [[501st Legion|stewardship]] of the Sith [[Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. Sidious subsequently assumed [[Dictatorship|absolute power]] as the [[Proclamation of the New Order|self-proclaimed]] [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. Clones initially served as '''[[Stormtrooper|Imperial stormtroopers]]''', or '''clone stormtroopers''', in the [[New Order]] but were [[Project War-Mantle|eventually]] [[Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill|replaced]] by [[TK stormtrooper|birth-born human recruits and conscripts]]. Their [[Clone trooper armor|armor]], weapons, and training inspired generations of [[armor]]ed warriors following on from their Imperial successors; with both the [[First Order]]'s [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtroopers]] and the [[Sith Eternal]]'s [[Sith trooper|red-armored soldiers]] having been [[Project Resurrection|trained]] from [[Youngling|early childhood]] to become super-soldiers much like the clone army. In particular, the latter were indoctrinated using a modified and improved upon version of the [[flash-training]] techniques previously used for the clones. ==History== ===Origin=== {{Quote|They are totally obedient, taking any order without question. We modified their genetic structure to make them less independent than the original host.''"
"''And who was the original host?''"
"''A bounty hunter called Jango Fett.|Lama Su and Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} [[Standard year|Years]] before the [[Invasion of Naboo]], [[Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas]] came to believe that [[the galaxy]] would soon become engulfed by war. He therefore advocated for the creation of an army to ensure the defense of the [[Galactic Republic]], but his views were ultimately rejected by his peers and he was cast out of the [[Jedi High Council]]. Undeterred by the lack of support from the other [[Jedi]], Sifo-Dyas secretly contacted the [[Kaminoan]]s{{Databank|sifo-dyas|Sifo-Dyas}}—a [[species]] of experts in [[cloning]], native to the [[planet]] [[Kamino]]—and commissioned them to create an army of clone [[soldier]]s for the Republic without authorization from either High Council or the [[Galactic Senate]]. Dyas personally met with the Kaminoan [[Prime Minister]], [[Lama Su]].''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' However, the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]] learned of Dyas' order through unknown means.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-the-creation-of-the-clone-army|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: The Creation of the Clone Army|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}} [[File:JangoFettMeetsWithDooku-AORJangoFett1.png|thumb|right|250px|Jango Fett was chosen by Sith apprentice Darth Tyranus to serve as the template for an army of clone troopers.]] The [[Sith apprentice]] [[Dooku|Darth Tyranus]], who was actually Sifo Dyas' friend and the former Jedi Master Dooku, later claimed Dyas had worked with him to create the clone army.{{TCW|The Lost One}} Shortly afterward, Sifo-Dyas was [[Death|killed]] by the [[Pyke Syndicate]] at the behest of the [[Sith]], resulting in the Sith's takeover of the clone trooper project. Tyranus betrayed and orchestrated Sifo Dyas' death, and subsequently recruited the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett]] to become the [[Clone template|genetic template]] of the clone army. Various modifications were made to the Fett [[DNA|genome]] so that the clones would grow faster and be more susceptible to following orders. Hyper-aggressive and volatile tendencies were tailored; the Kaminoans resorted to growth acceleration in order to create mature clones in half the [[time]] a [[human]] took to reach maturity. Fett's genetic structure was further modified to make the clones less independent and more docile than their template. However, the clones were also designed to be capable of creative thinking, making them far superior to [[battle droid]]s. After being created on Kamino,''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' some clones were secretly raised on [[Coruscant]] to become the [[Imperial shock trooper|shock troopers]] of the [[Coruscant Guard]]. Fett became a near-mythologized figure to his clones, who regarded him as their father figure.''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' Fett himself, however, did not feel a sense of pride in his clones, instead seeing them as "livestock" made to be "cannon fodder." As such, he considered them to be the Kaminoans' creations instead of his.[[Age of Republic - Jango Fett 1|''Age of Republic - Jango Fett'' 1]] [[File:Order66-SoH.png|thumb|left|250px|The Sith secretly guided the creation of the clone troopers on Kamino.]] Fett was paid a considerable amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for allowing the Kaminoans to use his genetic material as the clone army's template;{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/bounty-lost-episode-guide|text="Bounty Lost" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} his only other demand was the creation of an unaltered clone of himself, which the Kaminoans found unusual but nevertheless obliged. Whereas the clone army was genetically modified for growth acceleration and enhanced docility, [[Boba Fett|Alpha]]{{TBB|Bounty Lost}} was an example of pure genetic replication and therefore possessed pure, first generation Fett DNA. The only other clone like Alpha was an adolescent [[Gender|female]] known as [[Omega]].{{TBB|Aftermath (episode)}} Fett took Alpha to raise as his son, renaming the clone "Boba Fett." Omega remained in the custody of the Kaminoans and was serving as an [[aide]] of the [[Chief Medical Scientist]]{{TCW|Conspiracy}} [[Doctor]] [[Nala Se]] by the end of the [[Clone Wars]]. Like the rest of the Fett clones, they were regarded as Kaminoan property by Lama Su.{{TBB|Replacements}} Although the Kaminoans believed that the army was meant to serve the Republic, the Sith intended to use the clone troopers as their secret weapon against the [[Jedi Order]]. The clone army's true purpose was to exterminate the Jedi, and to that end, an organic [[Behavioral modification biochip|inhibitor chip]] was implanted into the brain of every clone trooper at the third stage of their development. Sifo-Dyas, who had originally thought of the chip, intended for it to be a safeguard against rogue Jedi, but following his death, Sidious and Tyranus retooled the chip to ensure the Jedi's destruction. Upon the activation of the retooled chip,{{TCW|Fugitive}} the clones would be brainwashed''[[Star Wars Journeys: Beginnings]]'' into believing that Jedi were traitors to the Republic, forcing the clones to execute the Jedi. Tyranus, who posed as a Jedi, tricked the Kaminoans into believing Sifo Dyas' intention. One chip failed in the case of [[Tup]], causing him to betray and kill a Jedi before the order was given. Officially, the chips were supposed to make the clones less aggressive and independent than Jango Fett. The significance of the inhibitor chip was supported by the assertion that a clone would become mentally unstable and dangerous to everyone around him if his chip was damaged or surgically removed.{{TCW|Orders (episode)}} The chips were, in fact, created to compel the clone troopers to execute [[Order 66]]—a secret protocol that authorized the destruction of the Jedi Order. [[File:Clone_cadet.svg|thumb|right|180px|The Kaminoan emblem was worn by all clones.]] Each clone trooper had an [[identifying code]] inserted in his left wrist. During the Clone Wars, the codes were linked to the file of every individual trooper in the Republic's military database. The files, which could be accessed by an [[astromech droid]] via the scanning of a clone's identifying code, contained the clones' designation, rank and overall service record, as well as any specialized training and the units that he was affiliated with.{{TCW|Missing in Action}} Most clones also shared their template's [[Color|dark-brown]] [[eye]]s, black [[hair]], and olive skin. While there were some genetic variations, most of these clones would ultimately remain confined to Kamino, being embarrassments or case studies. Only five clone anomalies remained by the end of the war, including Nala Se's assistant Omega, an enhanced female clone. The other four clones formed the original lineup of [[Clone Force 99]]. [[Hunter]], [[Tech]], [[Wrecker]], and [[Crosshair]] were genetically enhanced clones who possessed unique combat skills, setting them apart from the standard "reg" clone troopers as well as each other. [[File:Clonestraining.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The clone troopers were genetically identical as a result of originating from a single source of DNA.]] The term "generation one" designated the first group of clones who were created from{{TBB|Battle Scars}} the Jango Fett genotype, including [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] of the [[501st Legion]]{{Databank|clone-captain-rex|Clone Captain Rex}} and [[Clone Sergeant]] [[Slick]].Although Slick's name is not used in ''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]'', the book and the information it introduces clearly references the events of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[The Hidden Enemy]]" and Slick's actions within its story. Rex's service in the Clone Wars came to make him a legend amongst the troopers, with the captain eventually being regarded as the hero of the clone army.{{SW|url=battle-scars-episode-gallery|text="Battle Scars" Episode Gallery}} {{C|slide 5}} The first two-hundred thousand units were ready a decade after Sifo-Dyas commissioned the creation of the clone army. In addition to the first units, a million clones were being developed in the facilities spread across Kamino[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] at the time of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'s arrival. [[File:RexTroopers-Agenda.png|thumb|right|250px|Clone Captain Rex was a generation one clone who became the hero of the entire army.]] Kenobi discovered the clone project on Kamino and duly informed the Jedi High Council. By then, the galaxy was on the verge of a civil war between the Republic and a [[Separatist Crisis|secessionist movement]] that ultimately formed the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Since the Jedi lacked sufficient manpower to guard the entire Republic, the Senate resolved to grant emergency powers to the executive branch. As a result, the clone troopers were formally organized into the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] by [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine—the elected leader of the Senate and public persona of [[Darth]] Sidious, [[Dark Lord of the Sith]].{{Databank|sith|Sith}} With war imminent, [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] traveled to Kamino to personally inspect the clone army while Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]] led the [[Jedi assault team|vanguard]] against the Separatists on [[Geonosis]]. ===Clone Wars=== ====Soldiers of the Republic==== {{Quote|I have to admit that without the clones, it would have not been a victory.''"
"''Victory? Victory you say? Master Obi-Wan, not victory. The shroud of the dark side has fallen. Begun the Clone War has.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Yoda|}} [[File:SWL-Clone-Captain-Geonosis.png|thumb|left|300px|The deployment of clone troopers marked the beginning of the Clone Wars.]] Clone troopers were deployed into battle for the first time on the planet Geonosis, where twelve [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship|''Acclamator''-class assault ships]] supplied by Kamino were loaded with two battle armies, or 192,000 troops. Under the leadership of the Jedi, the Grand Army of the Republic forced the [[Separatist Droid Army]] into full retreat and consequently won the [[First Battle of Geonosis|first battle]] of the Clone Wars. With clones forming the backbone of the Republic's new military might, clone production on Kamino continued during the war due to the Republic's need for more soldiers.''[[Queen's Hope]]'' In the wake of the Republic victory on Geonosis, [[Count]] Dooku—the alter ego of Darth Tyranus—rallied a growing number of dissenting worlds to the Separatist cause, further dividing the Republic and forcing the clone troopers to fight the war on all fronts across the galaxy.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] Throughout the conflict, clone troopers continuously demonstrated extreme loyalty to the Galactic Republic, especially their [[Jedi General]]s and the Supreme Chancellor. The clones developed signs of individuality quickly, with the soldiers already showing themselves to be unique people during the first [[Standard week|weeks]] of the conflict. Despite the Kaminoans claiming it would hamper their effectiveness, Jedi [[General]] [[Plo Koon]] realized that the clones worked better as a unit when they were able to live out their individuality. Clones were expected by their brethren to be obedient to the chain of command, believing that their compliance reflected their commitment to the Republic. The [[Advanced Recon Commando]] [[Fives]] supported the system{{TCW|Plan of Dissent}} and was driven by his sense of duty as a loyal soldier of the Republic.{{TCW|Carnage of Krell}} [[File:KiAdiMundiGeonosis-LaPR.png|thumb|right|300px|Clone troopers served under the Knights of the Jedi Order, who held the rank of Jedi General in the Grand Army of the Republic.]] Fives also believed that clone troopers were not disposable "numbers" and as such he opposed complying with orders that he considered to be wrong, although [[Captain]] Rex maintained that a soldier should obey his [[commanding officer]] if he supported the system that they fought for. However, by the end of the bloody [[Battle of Umbara|Umbara Campaign]], Rex agreed with Fives, feeling that clones sometimes needed to disobey their orders in order to do what was right. While the clones were conditioned to be absolutely obedient, every clone developed his own unique identity. Insufficient or rushed field care led some clone veterans to have deep, physical scars. These soldiers wore their scars with pride, and some refused rehabilitative treatment to remove them.''[[Collapse of the Republic]]'' The distinction between each clone ranged from loyal units, such as [[Clone Commander]] [[Cody]]{{Databank|clone-commander-cody|Clone Commander Cody}} and Captain Rex, to a minority of clones who proved to be disloyal or uncommitted to the Republic's cause, such as [[Sergeant]] Slick. Regarding service as [[slavery]], Slick betrayed the Republic by accepting bribes from the Separatists and was therefore arrested as a [[Treason|traitor]] by the Grand Army.{{TCW|The Hidden Enemy}} [[File:Clone_Commander_CotR.png|thumb|left|220px|The clones adopted nicknames and new hairstyles as they became more individualistic.]] Another clone trooper displayed aberrant behavior by deserting the Grand Army and becoming a farmer under the name [[Cut Lawquane]], joining a [[Lawquane family|family]] on the planet [[Saleucami]].{{TCW|The Deserter}} Another clone deserter, [[Muzzle]], became head of the [[Aurodium Sword]] mercenary group. Through it, the clone continued to work with the Republic in a way, as the Aurodium Sword often took jobs as a security deal for Republic-aligned corporate personnel. Another clone deserted the military and took up a life that led them to a forest, where they wielded a [[rifle]].{{SWU|set=Shadows of the Galaxy|cardname=Clone Deserter|link=9503028597}} For the most part, however, the clones found pride in their purpose as soldiers, and many continued to sacrifice their lives for the Republic as the war wore on. Many of the clones that remained loyal throughout their service looked down on their brothers that had deserted, thinking them to be cowards or traitors. However, there were clones that were able to redeem themselves and willingly re-enter the ranks alongside their brothers. When a [[Heater's squad|squad]] of deserters were given the opportunity to leave the army after completing [[Assault on a Separatist weapons depot|one last mission]] together, the group came together and decided to remain in the army with their brothers.[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 4|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 4]] Alternatively, Rex decided against bringing Lawquane back to the Republic when they met face-to-face during the [[Battle of Saleucami]] in [[21 BBY]].{{TCWcanondates|210}} While he admitted it was supposed to be his duty to bring Lawquane in, he had fought beside the deserter and realized he was no coward, instead realizing that Lawquane was a man driven by a devotion to his family instead of the Republic. As such, Rex kept the secret of Lawquane's desertion to himself for the entire war.{{TBB|Cut and Run}} [[File:Rex_inspirational.png|thumb|right|250px|A sense of brotherhood existed among the clone troopers who had been bred to fight for the Galactic Republic.]] In addition to fighting alongside the Jedi and each other, the clone troopers viewed each other as brothers. While admirable, this quality could keep them from seeing the bigger picture and make them willfully ignorant of the Republic's politics, but such a feeling also made the clones family to each other,{{TCW|Victory and Death}} with troopers even using the word when talking to a fellow clone they had never met before.[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] To show her that she belonged among them, the clones who served alongside a trans female clone gave her the name [[Sister]]. Troopers also tended to see their [[barracks]] or [[starship]]s as places of work. In addition, the clones viewed Kamino as their [[homeworld]]. During the [[Battle of Kamino]], the clones fought bravely to prevent the Separatists from destroying the clone hatcheries as well as the remaining supply of their donor's genetic material. Their efforts resulted in a Republic victory, ensuring the continued production of clone troopers for the duration of the Clone Wars. As the Clone Wars dragged on, the stress of combat and high casualties caused cracks and strains among the ranks of the clone soldiers. Personality quirks, once considered harmless or even essential to their mental development, began to express themselves in extreme and polarizing ways. Each unit created their own rituals, small ways to identify squad mates, those from the same [[company]], and veterans of specific campaigns. A soldier that talked about "cracking that crystal" identified themselves as a veteran of [[Christophsis]] and the [[Battle of Christophsis|assault]] on [[Chaleydonia|Crystal City]], while an officer calling targets "bugs" revealed he fought in the hives on Geonosis. While many clones respected a soldier with a different background, some felt separated by time, space, and the unique aspects of their struggle. [[File:501stLegion-Umbara.png|thumb|left|280px|Some clone troopers questioned their purpose and wondered what would become of them after the Clone Wars.]] Though the vast majority of clones remained loyal to the Republic over the course of the three-year conflict, as time progressed a small number began to question their strict obedience. Naïve new clones found themselves fighting alongside veterans with years of combat experience that included the deaths of comrades, objectives gained and failed, and the often-ineffectual civilian Republic leadership. Consequently, some veterans developed a skepticism of Republic bureaucracy that shocked even the most cynical of rookie clones. Unlike most natural species where youth questioned their elders, it was the older clones of the Grand Army of the Republic who found themselves questioning their values and traditions. These clones still found comfort in the company of their brothers, but life no longer seemed as cut and dried to them. Many clones realized that they were not held in high regard among the Republic and were treated as expendable soldiers who did not have personal feelings. This would help clones grow closer to each other and those who went against this convention, notably Jedi Generals Plo Koon{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}} and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]].[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 5|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 5]] Although a divide of sorts existed between clones and Jedi, which was widened in the aftermath of General [[Pong Krell]]'s massacre of clone troopers during the [[Umbara]] Campaign,''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' clones remained very loyal to their leaders and generally considered them to be among their closest friends. Indeed, the troops were known to form friendships with their Jedi officers,[[Kanan 9|''Kanan'' 9]] especially those that demonstrated loyalty back to them. Among the Jedi who were highly respected was [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]],{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}} who believed all clones sounded different despite their genetic sameness; Yoda told her that was because she took the time needed to actually listen to them. Yoda also saw the clones as individuals, seeing that every trooper was different in the Force.{{TCW|Ambush}} ====Public image==== {{Quote|Valiant men, the clones have proven to be. Saved my life and yours they have many times. Believe in them we must.|Yoda|}} [[File:Boys_in_white.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Commission for the Protection of the Republic used clone troopers as wartime propaganda.]] Throughout the Clone Wars, clone troopers featured prominently in propaganda sponsored by both the Republic and Separatist media. The populist organization known as the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic]] (COMPOR) portrayed clones as the public face of the Republic's war effort, resulting in the publication of patriotic artwork such as ''[[Unite]]'' and ''[[Support the Boys in White]]''. The posters expressed patriotism and civic duty to the citizens of the Republic. Part of a large outreach campaign, clone troopers became the symbol of the war effort, largely replacing the Jedi of previous years. Projecting strength and unity, they reminded citizens that their sacrifices were funding peace through military might.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' Action figures of the clones were sold for children.{{SW|url=andor-s1-e5-trivia-gallery|text="The Axe Forgets" Trivia Gallery | Andor}} {{C|Slide 1}} With there being significant debate amongst the public about the morality of sending living beings against an army of droids at the start of the war, COMPOR's messages were intended to ingrain the image of the clone trooper as brave soldiers risking all for freedom, democracy and the Republic. Such was ironic given that the clones themselves enjoyed few individual liberties.''[[Star Wars Made Easy]]'' Although COMPOR also wanted to use the Jedi Order as a tool for propaganda, Chancellor Palpatine advised against this course of action, citing sympathy for the Jedi's reluctant acceptance of their new role during wartime. As a result, very few [[Jedi Unite for Peace|examples]] of pro-Jedi messages exist as COMPOR devoted their full attention to promoting support for the clone troopers as well as loyalty to the Republic and, in particular, Chancellor Palpatine. [[File:Anti-Jedi_protest_signs.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Civilians protested Jedi and clones alike, believing both groups were responsible for prolonging the conflict.]] By contrast, the Confederacy of Independent Systems decried the clone army as a biological abomination—an inhumane practice in which weaponized embryos were carried to artificial term and turned into disposable killing machines. The Separatist cause was, therefore, portrayed as the more "humane" approach due to the Confederacy's use of battle droids. In some way, this dehumanizing sentiment was shared in the Republic. Under Republic law, clone troopers were property of the Galactic Republic. However, Nala Se took the position that the clones were Kaminoan property, as they had been created in the laboratories of Kamino. Senator [[Christo]] of the Galactic Senate considered the clones disposable, supported increasing the cloning production, and rationalized their deaths as the fulfillment of their purpose.{{TCW|Pursuit of Peace}} An [[anti-clone sentiment]] persisted after the war's end and into the [[Imperial Era]].{{TBB|The Summit}} Galactic citizens could also be unaware of the friendships that could grow between clones and Jedi; [[farmer]] [[Kaeden Larte]] believed clones only followed Jedi like Ahsoka Tano because they were superior officers, unaware of how Jedi like Tano had truly earned the troopers' respect. As the war carried on, more Republic citizens became disillusioned with the seemingly endless conflict, allowing Separatist and antiwar propaganda to take root in the Republic's territory. Widespread discontent began to erode the clones' public image despite COMPOR's efforts; even their civilian-coined nickname "Boys in White" backfired as antiwar activists pointed to the fact that the clones were barely thirteen years old by the third year of the Clone Wars. ===Order 66=== ====Sith conspiracy==== {{Quote|I like a good mystery.''"
"''Yeah? You ever hear the one about the people engineered to kill, engineered to kill their best friends, their leaders, and they don't even know it?|[[Jay Igno]] and Fives|}} [[File:PrematureExecution-TU.png|thumb|right|250px|The Sith conspiracy against the Jedi was jeopardized by a defective clone that prematurely executed Order 66.]] Near the end of the war, Order 66 was nearly discovered by the Jedi. Tup was a clone trooper in the 501st [[Legion]] who became mentally unstable when his inhibitor chip malfunctioned during the [[Battle of Ringo Vinda]], causing him to betray and kill Jedi [[General]] [[Tiplar]].{{TCW|The Unknown}} This premature execution of Order 66 resulted in an investigation by the Republic, the Jedi, and the Kaminoans. The Sith also took an interest in the matter; Count Dooku—whom Lama Su and Nala Se knew only as "Tyranus," their secret benefactor—instructed the Kaminoans to prevent the Jedi from discovering the true purpose of the inhibitor chips. Tyranus was also disturbed by the degree of individuality that the clones displayed in spite of their psychological conditioning; Nala Se believed that the Jedi were responsible for encouraging greater creative thinking in the clones. Nevertheless, she was certain that, with the exception of Tup's damaged chip, the rest of the chips would function according to their design. [[File:CoruscantGuardssearching.png|thumb|left|250px|The Coruscant Guard was deployed to hunt Fives, a clone framed for treason.]] During the investigation, the ARC trooper Fives became increasingly convinced that the inhibitor chip was part of a conspiracy against the Republic and the Jedi. Against Nala Se's advice, he was allowed to plead his case to Chancellor Palpatine. However, their meeting led the ARC trooper to believe that the Chancellor was involved in the conspiracy, although he was unaware of to what extent. Jedi Master [[Shaak Ti]] witnessed Fives' attempt to assassinate the Chancellor and prevented him from succeeding. Although Fives [[Escape from the Grand Republic Medical Facility|escaped]] from the [[Grand Imperial Medical Facility|Grand Republic Medical Facility]], he was confronted by a group of Coruscant shock troopers led by Clone [[Commander]] [[Fox]] while attempting to warn Jedi General [[Anakin Skywalker]] and Captain Rex. After Fives was killed by Fox, Palpatine convinced the Jedi that a rare parasite from [[Ringo Vinda]] was responsible for the malfunction in Tup and Fives, and that the clone troopers had to be inoculated to prevent their inhibitor chips from malfunctioning. Shortly before dying, Tup and Fives—both of whom had their chips removed—described Order 66 as a mission that they repeatedly experienced in their nightmares. With their deaths and the removal of any evidence that could alert the Jedi to the existence of Order 66, the Chancellor convinced the Jedi Council that the clone troopers did require their inhibitor chips. Still, Rex, who had held Fives as he died, submitted a grievance report, where he stated the inhibitor chips could have an alternate purpose. While he was not sure if he believed it and knew the report would be ignored, Rex believed he owed it to Fives to record what he had learned. [[File:GoodbyeFives-O.png|thumb|right|250px|Fives was killed before he could expose the plot to turn the clone troopers against their Jedi Generals.]] The death of Fives did not completely ensure the secrecy of Order 66, however. The Jedi Council began inquiring into the specific circumstances regarding the mysterious death of Sifo-Dyas, the founder of the clone army. Alarmed by the Jedi's interest in the matter, Darth Sidious tasked his apprentice with the responsibility of eliminating any remaining loose ends that could connect the Sith with the creation of the clones. Darth Tyranus journeyed to the planet [[Oba Diah]] and killed [[Minister]] [[Lom Pyke]] of the [[Pyke]] Syndicate, but not before the Pyke revealed to the Jedi that Tyranus and Dooku were one and the same. The Jedi Council was disturbed by the revelation of the Sith Order's involvement in the creation of the clones. Yet in spite of their suspicions regarding the reasons the Sith would provide the Jedi with an army, the Council ultimately chose to conceal their findings from the public and the government, fearing that such a discovery would undermine public confidence in the war. Grand Master Yoda insisted that their priority remained the same, to end the war as swiftly as possible before the Sith's plans came to fruition. Moreover, the Grand Master believed that the clones were genuinely loyal to their Jedi leaders, having saved them on numerous occasions throughout the war. ====Fall of the Jedi==== {{Quote|How widespread is this?''"
"''Ahsoka, it's all of us. The entire Grand Army of the Republic has been ordered to hunt down and destroy the Jedi Knights.|Ahsoka Tano and Rex, on Order 66|audio=HowWidespread-Shattered.flac|}} [[File:212th_Battalion.png|thumb|left|250px|Utapau was invaded by the Republic clone army, their objective to destroy General Grievous and end the Clone Wars.]] After three years of constant warfare, the Separatist forces [[Battle of Coruscant|attacked]] the Republic [[capital]] world{{Databank|coruscant|Coruscant}} of Coruscant and managed to abduct Chancellor Palpatine in the process, a plan which was organized by Sidious in order to bring Anakin to the dark side and make him his apprentice. By the time of the battle, a full third of the original deployment of clones had been killed in action. Those who survived wore armor that had been dirtied and dented by conflict.''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' The clone troopers rallied to Coruscant's defense while the Jedi Knights Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker rescued the Chancellor. During the battle, Darth Tyranus was betrayed by Sidious, who swayed Skywalker to killing him. With Dooku dead, this brought the Clone Wars closer to a successful conclusion for the Republic. The Jedi Council moved to capitalize on the momentum gained by Tyranus' death in the hope of ending the war. The Grand Army continued to fight the war on various worlds across the galaxy, including [[Mygeeto]], [[Felucia]], [[Cato Neimoidia]], and [[Saleucami]]. New fronts were opened as clone troopers were deployed to [[Kashyyyk]] and [[Utapau]]; and other planets as part of the [[Outer Rim Sieges]]. [[Gree (clone trooper)|Gree]] and the [[41st Elite Corps]] fought side-by-side with the [[Wookiee]]s in the [[Battle of Kashyyyk]], under the command of Yoda, while Kenobi and Cody oversaw the [[Battle of Utapau]] between the [[212th Attack Battalion]] and General [[Grievous]]'s [[droid]] army. Unknown to all, however, the Outer Rim Sieges and associated hunt for Grievous were designed by Sidious to divide the Jedi Order on numerous fronts, emptying the Jedi Temple and leaving the Jedi out in the field, where they were joined only by their trusted clone troopers.''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' By this time, the [[332nd Division]] had been formed out of Skywalker's 501st Legion in order to participate in the [[Siege of Mandalore]]. The new division was placed under the command of Rex, who was promoted to the rank of Clone Commander, while Skywalker's former Padawan, the [[Force-Sensitive Outcast]] Tano, accompanied the 332nd as an [[advisor]]. [[File:Execute_Order_66.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Sidious contacted Clone Commander Cody, as well as other clone officers, and instructed them to execute Order 66.]] As the Republic drew closer to achieving total victory in the Clone Wars, Chancellor Palpatine revealed his deception and true identity as Darth Sidious to the Jedi, provoking an immediate response from the Jedi Council. The consequent [[Duel in Palpatine's office|confrontation]] between the Council and the Dark [[Lord]] ended in the deaths of several Jedi Masters, including Mace Windu, and Skywalker's fall to the [[dark side of the Force]]. Now anointed as the Sith Lord Darth Vader, Sidious' new apprentice participated in the 501st Legion's [[Operation: Knightfall|assault]] on the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]]. Under the influence of Order 66, the 501st clone troopers stormed the Temple and exterminated the Jedi within. None of the Jedi were spared, including the [[youngling]]s. Some clone troopers then donned Jedi robes as [[Disguised Clone Trooper|disguised Jedi]] to entrap any Jedi who tried to enter the building.''[[Revenge of the Sith - The Film Novel]]'' Around the same time, Darth Sidious issued Order 66 to the clone troopers throughout the galaxy—declaring every Jedi an enemy of the Republic. Order 66 triggered the hidden chips within the clones, erasing their loyalty to the Jedi and brainwashing them into believing that the Jedi were traitors to the Republic who deserved execution. Losing their freewill and identities with the mere activation of a chip through a voice command, the overwhelming majority of the clones suddenly turned on their unsuspecting allies; caught off guard by their own troops betraying them, the Jedi across numerous worlds were largely slaughtered by their clone troopers. However, there were a handful of clones that resisted the command by removing their biochips. The members of Clone Force 99, excluding Crosshair, did not obey the command as well, as their genetic enhancements made them immune to their chips. With the exception of a few survivors, the Jedi were all but extinct in the aftermath of the initial execution of Order 66. In addition, this protocol did not end with members of the Jedi Order, as clone troopers who failed to comply with the order were to be killed as well. [[File:Order66Ahsoka-Shattered.png|thumb|left|250px|Across the galaxy, the clone troopers turned against their Jedi leaders as a result of their programmed compliance with Order 66.]] Aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Tribunal]]'',''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' Tano and the rogue Sith Lord Darth [[Maul]] were [[Skirmish aboard the Tribunal|also targeted]] by the clones of the 332nd Division shortly after their victory on [[Mandalore]]. Commander Rex managed to resist his chip's control for long enough to tell Tano to find Fives. When Rex finally fell victim to its control, Tano escaped the troopers and released Maul from [[Mandalorian vault|captivity]], intending to have him be a distraction. Tano then looked into Fives, finding Rex's grievance report on the chips. With the help of astromech droids [[R7-A7]], [[CH-33P]], and [[RG-G1]], Tano incapacitated Rex in order to remove his chip, which restored his loyalty to Ahsoka. Freed from the influence of the control chip, Rex informed Tano that the entire Grand Army had turned against the Jedi. The former Jedi, the Clone Commander, and the astromech droids planned to steal a [[shuttle]] from the Venator's main hangar; Rex complied with Tano's wishes to only stun the clones in their path, despite knowing that his brethren fully intended to execute them as traitors to the state. Elsewhere, Maul continued to move through the [[warship]], ultimately entering and destroying the [[hyperdrive]] room. This pulled the [[Star Destroyer]] out of [[hyperspace]] and into the gravitational field of a [[Unidentified moon|moon]], but the 332nd remained determined to kill Tano, even if it would result in their own deaths.
