You think you're some kind of Jedi, waving your hand around like that? I'm a Toydarian, mind tricks don't work on me. Only money. No money, no parts, no deal!|Watto|audio=JediToydarianNoTricksNoDeal-TPM.flac|}} '''Watto''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[Toydarian]] [[junk dealer]] and [[human]] trafficker who owned a [[Watto's junkshop|junkshop]] in [[Mos Espa]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He was the owner of [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]] as well as her son, [[Anakin Skywalker]], the young [[Youngling|boy]] who would grow up to become both a revered [[Jedi Knight]] and a feared [[Sith]] [[Sith Lord|Lord]] known as [[Darth]] Vader. ==Biography== ===Fall of the Republic=== Watto started his life as a [[soldier]] on [[Toydaria]]. However, he left Toydaria after he suffered an injury and went to [[Tatooine]], where he watched [[Jawa]]s sell used goods and decided to start his own business.''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' [[File:Qui-Gon_mind_trick.png|thumb|left|250px|Qui-Gon Jinn attempting to perform a mind trick on Watto]] Watto became a [[junk dealer]] living in [[Mos Espa]] where he owned a small [[Watto's junkshop|shop]]. Watto won two [[Slavery|slaves]], [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]] and her son [[Anakin Skywalker|Anakin]], from [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder|Gardulla]] the [[Hutt]] in a bet. Watto discovered Anakin's natural [[podracing]] abilities and began to sponsor the [[Gender|boy]] in several Podraces. Despite this, Watto often bet against Anakin. Watto would also host podracing viewing parties for his gambling partners and friends in his [[Watto's box|private box]]. Aside from maintaining droids, Watto also had Anakin polish their parts[[Age of Republic - Anakin Skywalker 1|''Age of Republic - Anakin Skywalker'' 1]] and clean his shop. On one occasion, Watto berated Skywalker as he tried to clean the floors with a brush.[[Age of Rebellion - Darth Vader 1|''Age of Rebellion - Darth Vader'' 1]] At another point, Watto demanded Skywalker continue polishing a droid's headpiece until it reflected his face. In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' the [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] came to his store looking for parts for his ship. Jinn did not have enough money and was unable to negotiate a price with Watto, even failing to perform a [[mind trick]] on the [[Toydarian]]. [[File:Wattomocks.png|thumb|right|250px|Watto observing the Boonta Eve podracing event]] The next [[Standard day|day]], Jinn told Watto that he wanted to enter Anakin in the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] in exchange for parts for his ship. Watto agreed and entered Anakin but Watto bet on the [[Dug]] [[racer]] [[Sebulba]]. Jinn placed a bet for Anakin's freedom despite Watto's warnings that Anakin was going to lose anyway. Anakin, however, won the race and left Tatooine with Jinn to become a [[Jedi]] on [[Coruscant]] while Shmi remained with Watto. Years later, Watto sold Shmi to the [[moisture farmer]] [[Cliegg Lars]], who bought her to live with him on his [[Lars homestead|moisture farm]],{{Film|II}} after he lost a gambling game to the farmer. In truth, Shmi had plotted her freedom with the [[Lars family]], telling Cliegg and the others about Watto's weakness to gambling.''[[Queen's Hope]]'' Four years after the Invasion of Naboo, [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] sent her handmaiden [[Sabé]] to track down Shmi and free as many slaves as she could. Sabé was unsuccessful in tracking down Watto or Shmi, being forced to instead waste time dealing with Watto's associates.''[[Queen's Shadow]]'' During all these years, Watto continued with his faithful trade and even bought adjacent buildings to enlarge his shop, but he started to suffer great losses on gambling, leaving the future of his business unsure, aside from that he had no longer the necessary personnel and was forced to do all the hard work himself.[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] [[File:Watto-old.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Watto shortly before the Clone Wars]] In [[22 BBY]], shortly before the [[First Battle of Geonosis|beginning]] of the [[Clone Wars]], Anakin returned to Tatooine in search of his mother. Watto, after recognizing his former slave, asked him if he could help with some "deadbeats" who owed him a lot of money. After being asked about Shmi, Watto gave him all of the information he knew about Shmi after selling her. In the end, Skywalker would [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars|reach his mother]] just as she passed on, to which he responded by slaughtering the [[Tusken Raider]]s who had taken her prisoner in a major step in his journey into the [[dark side of the Force]] and transformation into the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader. His time as a slave under the likes of Watto[[Legacy of Vader 2|''Legacy of Vader'' 2]] and the way in which he could be treated also played a role in forging Skywalker into Vader. ===Age of the Empire and legacy=== [[File:VaderFlames-LegacyOfVader2.png|thumb|right|300px|Watto unknowingly played a role in creating the Sith Lord Darth Vader, who wreaked havoc upon the galaxy.]] During his [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] on Tatooine after [[Order 66]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] purchased a humidifier from Watto at an inflated price. After Kenobi was [[Rescue of Princess Leia|killed]] by Vader on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]]{{StoryCite|story=Time of Death|book=From a Certain Point of View}} in [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' Kenobi, who had unlocked the secret to preserving himself after death, found himself in a vision of his [[Ben Kenobi's home|hut]] on Tatooine. He noted that the humidifier was not in the vision, among other recent additions that were missing. He then realized the vision was of an earlier time in his hut, from around three years into his exile. Vader, meanwhile, would continue serving the [[Galactic Empire]] until his return to the light side and subsequent death in [[4 ABY]]. He was survived by his son, [[Luke Skywalker]], and daughter, [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], who herself would have a son named [[Ben Solo]] with her husband [[Han Solo]]. All the while, Vader's servant [[Vaneé]] stayed hidden in his late master's [[Fortress Vader|castle]] on the planet [[Mustafar]][[Legacy of Vader 1|''Legacy of Vader'' 1]] and used Vader's security codes to access files kept by [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], Vader's [[Sith Master]] whom the redeemed [[Jedi]] had slain upon his return to the light. In reading Palpatine's files, Vaneé learned much about his fallen master, including his time as a slave on Tatooine under Gardulla and Watto, much to his fascination. By [[34 ABY]],{{YouTube|video=0Mp3MNsQVDQ|text=The FUTURE of Star Wars Comics - An Interview With Charles Soule, Marc Guggenheim, and Alex Segura|channel=@StarWarsExplained|name=Star Wars Explained}} establishes that the events of ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of Vader]]'' take place immediately after the events of {{Film|VIII}}, which takes place in [[34 ABY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. the shop once owned by Watto in Mos Espa sat in ruins. In that year, Ben—by that point living under the name "Kylo Ren" and reigning as the [[Supreme Leader]] of the [[First Order]]—traveled to Tatooine with Vaneé, who hoped to show Vader's grandson how the man's past had forged him into a powerful Sith Lord. Teaching Ren of how Skywalker had once been a slave, Vaneé brought Ren to the ruins of Watto's shop; the damage to the site made Ren theorize about and imagine his grandfather returning to the place he had once been enslaved to enact revenge upon Watto, whom he imagined being slain with a Force choke. However, Vaneé confirmed that Vader had not killed Watto as the Sith Lord had other matters to focus on, but he did reveal Gardulla still lived, much to Ren's anger. Ren quickly departed from Watto's ruined shop to slay the Hutt who had once enslaved his grandfather. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Outlanders. They think we know nothing.|translated=1|Watto|}} [[File:Wattos_Chance_Cube_SoH.png|thumb|left|270px|Watto was an avid gambler.]] Watto was proud of his business and distrusting of [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], which he felt were not "real" enough for the tough economy of an [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim Territory]] [[planet]] like Tatooine. When Qui-Gon Jinn attempted a mind trick on him in order to get him to accept 20,000 credits in exchange for a [[T-14 hyperdrive generator]], he shrugged it off, telling Jinn that as a Toydarian, mind tricks did not work on him. Watto was a heavy gambler, and later lost the hyperdrive and Anakin in a bet he had wagered against the Jedi. After Anakin's departure, he started to suffer heavy losses on gambling. As the owner of Shmi and Anakin Skywalker, Watto was not a particularly kind master, even though the living conditions of the Skywalkers were more agreeable in comparison to their life in servitude to Gardulla the Hutt. However, Watto sometimes showed flashes of compassion: he allowed Anakin to go home early if he finished all his assigned tasks and Shmi to perform certain quieter duties at the comfort of her private work station.''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]'' Watto's underestimation of Anakin proved to be a heavy blow to his business. Once Anakin left Tatooine and after he sold Shmi to the [[Lars family]], Watto found himself with no help and was forced to do the hard job himself so his business could survive. Ill-used to the huge capabilities of his former slave, Watto was not able to find anymore servants with the sufficient technical knowledge. ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== [[File:Watto-SWE.png|thumb|right|250px|Watto as seen in ''The Phantom Menace'']] Watto was portrayed and voiced by actor [[Andrew Secombe]] in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] and its [[2002]] sequel [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. Secombe played Watto on set, to give animators a reference for lighting and eye-line.[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] Conceived by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]], Watto's design was more avian in nature, featuring plumage and a beak. Later incarnations of the Toydarian featured a cigar and tentacles.{{DB|location|wattosshop|Watto's shop}} When artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] began designing the character, she began with an ugly, "cherub-like" design. Lucas suggested that he be given webbed, duck-like feet. Eventually, the basis for the character's face was derived from an early concept painting of the [[Neimoidian]] race by concept artist [[Doug Chiang]], particularly the hooked trunk and the crooked teeth. As the character spoke frequently, animator [[Rob Coleman]] found lip-syncing Watto's lines with Secombe's delivery of the dialog to be difficult. To solve the issue, Coleman had part of Watto's teeth chipped away, so the character could speak out the side of his mouth, making the syncing process much easier. Sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] recorded himself opening and closing an umbrella to make the sound of Watto's wings flapping. Watto was given a son, [[Blatto]],{{Twitter|hellofathead|status/484904403414310912|[[Robert F. Hughes|Robert F Hughes]]|date=2014-07-04|quote=@hulitherium @animag @rwmead @DanPovenmire @mmonogram that's Watto's son, Blatto.}} {{C|In response to: "@animag @rwmead Whoa, is that Watto? If it is then that's pretty cool. @DanPovenmire @mmonogram @hellofathead"}} in the [[Canon|non-canon]] television special ''[[Phineas and Ferb: Star Wars]]''.''[[Phineas and Ferb: Star Wars]]'' ===Legacy of Vader=== {{Quote|Memories! You have to remember the good times.|Charles Soule, on Watto|{{Twitter|CharlesSoule|status/1883604646390108606|[[Charles Soule]]|quote=Was utterly delighted to find this in my timeline. Memories! You have to remember the good times.}}}} [[File:Charles-and-Watto.png|thumb|left|250px|Author Charles Soule poses with a Watto cosplayer]] Ahead of the release of [[Legacy of Vader 2|''Legacy of Vader'' 2]],{{Twitter|markpaniccia|status/1882799792323244050|[[Mark Paniccia]]|quote=Sneak peeks of STAR WARS: LEGACY OF VADER #2. Kylo Ren on... Tatooine!}} a comic issue written by [[Charles Soule]] and illustrated by [[Luke Ross]] released on [[March 12]], [[2025]],{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/119563/star_wars_legacy_of_vader_2025_2|text=Star Wars: Legacy of Vader (2025) #2}} [[Marvel Comics]] senior editor [[Mark Paniccia]] shared images from the issue on [[January 24]], including a piece depicting Vader Force choking Watto as another character—established to be Kylo Ren in the issue itself—proclaims that the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] must have returned to Tatooine for revenge at one point. Many fans took the scene as confirmation that Watto was killed by Vader, a claim which went viral{{WebCite|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2025/01/darth-vader-watto-meme-star-wars|text=Darth Vader randomly killing Watto turned into hysterical Star Wars meme|author=Woodroof, Cory|date=2025-01-25|work=[[Wikipedia:USA Today|USA Today]]|archivedate=20250126022907}}{{WebCite|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/danidiplacido/2025/01/26/darth-vader-killed-watto-and-star-wars-fans-dont-know-how-to-feel|text=Darth Vader Killed Watto—And 'Star Wars' Fans Don't Know How To Feel|author=Placido, Dani Di|date=2025-01-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Forbes|Forbes]]|archivedate=20250127045953}} and was repeated as a fact in online news articles{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-canon-darth-vader-kills-watto-factoid|text=Murder Is Wrong, But Star Wars Just Dealt Watto the Death He Always Deserved|author=Wrenn, Jenna|date=2025-01-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|Screen Rant]]|archivedate=20250125035643}}{{WebCite|url=https://www.thepopverse.com/comics-star-wars-legacy-of-vader-2-comic-charles-soule-luke-ross-darth-kylo-ren-watto-phantom-menace|text=It is now Star Wars canon that Anakin Skywalker murdered the hell out of Watto|author=DeArmitt, Grant|date=2025-01-24|work=''Popverse''|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/CUO5E}}{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/star-wars-watto-death-darth-vader-marvel-comics-2000554578|text=''Star Wars''{{'s}} Newest Comics Will Give Watto the Death He Deserves|author=Whitbrook, James|date=2025-01-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|Gizmodo]]|archivedate=20250124173145}} and [[Wikipedia:Internet meme|Internet memes]]. Soule, however, urged fans to be careful about assuming story details from preview panels.{{Bluesky|charlessoule.bsky.social|post/3lgl3ojakls2j|[[Charles Soule]]|date=2025-01-25|quote=(Unless I'm posting it, wait until you see the final issue before assuming any posted preview panels or plot summaries from comics I write represent what actually happens. Or don't! Have fun with it!)}} Soule also responded to the discussion around Watto's apparent death by quote-[[Wikipedia:Twitter|tweeting]] an old picture of himself with a Watto cosplayer and reposting it to his [[Wikipedia:Bluesky|Bluesky account]], reflecting the "happier,"{{Bluesky|charlessoule.bsky.social|post/3lgo6sa3dic2x|[[Charles Soule]]|date=2025-01-26|quote=In happier times…}} "good times" they had shared. In his [[January 28]] newsletter, Soule further reflected on the online reaction to Watto's apparent demise, expressing his surprise at how emotionally attached the internet was to Watto and thanking fans for the many memes that had come out of it, which he found hilarious. He also pointed in particular to a [[Wikipedia:Forbes|''Forbes'']] article{{EmailCite|email=File:CharlesSoule-TrialsNewsletter.png|creator=Charles Soule|date=2025-01-28}} by writer Dani Di Placido for its coverage of Watto's demise and inclusion of fan memes. According to Soule in the newsletter, Watto's apparent death was a key moment in ''Legacy of Vader'' 2. When the issue released, it was revealed that Watto's apparent murder was Kylo's assumption that Vader had returned to kill him, which [[Vaneé]] confirmed was not the case. ===LEGO=== ====Droid tales and tales of terror==== {{Quote|Red flags! Premiering in [[2016]], the first episode, "[[Exit from Endor]]," adapts the events of ''The Phantom Menace'' and ''Attack of the Clones''. On Tatooine, Watto vigorously advertises big red flags as Qui-Gon Jinn offers Anakin Skywalker the opportunity to become a Jedi. During a victory celebration on Naboo, Watto promotes flashing danger signs as Queen Padmé Amidala tells young Skywalker she wants to see more of him. In "[[Gambit on Geonosis]]", Watto aids Anakin's son, Luke, during his [[rescue of Han Solo]], taking part in a human pyramid.{{DroidTales|Gambit on Geonosis}} In the [[2021]] Halloween special ''[[LEGO Star Wars Terrifying Tales]]'', the [[Sith cultist]] [[Vaneé]] tells [[Dean (mechanic)|Dean]], a young [[Technician|mechanic]] stranded at [[Fortress Vader]], the story of The Wookiee's Paw. In it, Watto overhears a disgruntled Luke Skywalker, who desires to leave Tatooine.
